reason: The statewide, season-long surveillance contains separable high-school soccer concussion findings and a mappable clinical definition, but it calculates incidence only from athletic participant counts per 100 player-seasons. It reports no time exposure, athlete-exposures, match-exposures, valid published time rate, or defensible derivation inputs.

This two-page BJSM PhD Academy Award item is an editorial-style thesis summary, not a report of one primary study or a declared eligible systematic review. It describes a thesis and cites the underlying articles rather than supplying a study-specific methods-and-results report for extraction.

Despite the word 'football' in the title, the cohort is NCAA Football Bowl Subdivision American football. The paper's comparison with soccer occurs only in the Introduction and does not supply a separable association-football dataset.

The source is the Danish National Patient Registry, supplemented by a retrospective questionnaire of registered patients and population/athlete registry figures. It does not report prospectively collected injury outcomes from current participating football teams or their clinical staff. Its sport-specific metric is per 100,000 registered athletes, not an eligible exposure denominator.

This two-page BJSM PhD Academy Award item summarises four thesis articles, including an underlying trial and secondary analysis, rather than reporting a single study's full methods and results. It is neither the underlying primary paper nor a declared eligible systematic/scoping/umbrella review or meta-analysis in its own right.
